lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet camps can hide a loud idea, and Toronto's newest one is easy to hear: Gavin McKenna will spend his first NHL season living with John Tavares. That off-ice handoff, confirmed Tuesday, is the most telling Maple Leafs development of the week - a veteran No. 1 pick taking the league's latest under his roof. The Leafs are in the deep offseason and their season is over, but this is how a team retools without the brass band: give the kid a guide, give the room a spine, and hope the lessons travel as fast as the puck. Tavares is entering his 18th NHL season, and McKenna arrives after 15 goals and 51 points in 35 games at Penn State. What matters next is September camp, when Toronto finds out how much of its future can be fast-tracked now.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays have stopped tiptoeing and started swinging - and Kazuma Okamoto's 30th homer and José Soriano's seven sharp innings in a 4-2 win over the Athletics gave the club a clean jolt when it needed one. Toronto is 73-73, a flat record that leaves no room for self-pity, only urgency, and Okamoto has become the bat that changes the shape of the lineup by the night. Soriano, meanwhile, looked like a man who belonged at the front of a staff, not in the middle of a muddle. That matters now because the Jays' next chapter will be written by young power, health, and roster clarity - not nostalgia. What to watch next is whether the front office can turn that September spark into an offseason blueprint.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Quiet doesn't mean inert in Toronto. It means the waiting has gotten louder - especially with Kawhi Leonard in Miami at the Raptors' organized minicamp, limited to individual workouts while the trade stays stuck in neutral. That's the whole story right now: a club in the deep offseason, a deal that still hasn't been signed off, and a fan base peering past the static for a real roster shape. Jack Armstrong's contract limbo only adds to the uncertainty around the edges. The Raptors are finished with last season and staring at camp later this month; what matters now is whether Leonard officially lands, and how quickly the picture sharpens around him. Watch the paperwork, watch the September 28 media day, and watch whether Toronto can turn this holding pattern into a proper start.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The line that matters is still the one in front of Jayden Daniels - and it's ugly. Washington opened its week with Nick Allegretti installed at center on the first depth chart, while Jacory Croskey-Merritt sits atop the backfield, a pairing that says the Commanders are betting on grit, coaching and improvisation up front. The record is history now; the job is to keep Daniels upright after an offseason that turned the line into a weekly stress test. Allegretti's calf trouble and Laremy Tunsil's absence have made the middle of the pocket look thinner than a paper dollar. Croskey-Merritt, no longer the cute story, has to be a real runner. What to watch next: whether Washington's patched-together front can hold through the opener and give this offense a fair start.

article.title: Tavares Opens Home, Kawhi Returns
paragraphs: John Tavares says Gavin McKenna will live with him during the 2026-27 season, a small but notable sign of how the Maple Leafs are shaping their next wave. For the Blue Jays, the morning note is more immediate: Sportsnet says Soriano set the tone as Toronto bounced back from a sloppy loss, while Bluebird Banter reported a Jays win over the A's.

The Raptors have a more curious offseason thread, with reports that Kawhi Leonard is taking part in an organized minicamp of Raptors players and has also been working out with the team in Miami. For the Commanders, camp-watch continues around Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who is no longer playing with house money as roster decisions sharpen.
